newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury starts first full day with new member.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury starts first full day with new member.

text.p: The newly constituted jury in O.J. Simpson's civil trial began its first full day of deliberations on Monday with no indication of when a verdict would be reached.

Jurors were under orders from Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki to start from scratch on Friday after he removed the panel's only black member and replaced her with an alternate. The original panel had debated for about 14 hours over three days last week.

Rosemary Caraway was removed from the jury after Fujisaki learned she had failed to disclose that her daughter worked in the Los Angeles County District Attorney's office. She was replaced by an Asian man in his 30s who works as a computer programmer.
The six-woman, six-man jury now includes nine whites, one Asian, one Hispanic and one man who is part-black, part-Asian.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, in October 1995. He is now battling a wrongful-death lawsuit filed by the victims families, who are seeking substantial damages.
